exposure: help-seeking behaviour (at pregnancy and 1 month postpartum)
sources of social support (at 3 months postpartum)
paternal involvement in feeding and changing diapers
number of hours of antenatal class attended (for multiparous)
parental satisfaction at 3 months postpartum (for multiparous)
cohort: A total of 209 mothers aged 21 years and above, with low socioeconomic status and irrespective of parity, were recruited from a local hospital.
finding: First-time mothers with low socioeconomic status who underwent caesarean section, did not attend antenatal classes, and had husbands uninvolved in infant care were significantly less likely to seek help at 3 months postpartum.
mod_finding: Primiparous mothers with low socioeconomic status who underwent caesarean section exhibited less help-seeking behaviours at 3 months postpartum.
